newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed ahead of Wall St opening.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed ahead of Wall St opening.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed on Monday in thin trading as investors awaited Wall Street's opening, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 0.11 percent, or 0.32 points, to 294.68 on low all-share turnover of 161 million shekels against 165 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.15 percent higher at 303.13.

"Everyone was waiting today for Wall Street opening," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI). "Investors were sitting on the fence waiting to see if the American market would recover from Friday's slide."
The Dow Jones industrial average sank 247 points on Friday in the second-biggest point loss in its history, causing Tel Aviv-traded shares to fall sharply on Sunday.
"Now the mood has improved as higher futures reflect expectations for a recovery of the U.S. stock market," said Daniel Werker-Barak of Ofek Securities.

"Despite the fact that the market lost two percent on Sunday there is no hysteria. The market wants to continue rising and only Wall Street is preventing it right now from doing so," the FIBI trader said.

"The strength of the bond market supports the positive trend of the stock market and if nothing dramatic happens on Wall Street the market is expected to resume its positive momentum," Werker-Barak said.

He added that the Bank of Israel would likely raise interest rates 0.3 percentage point later this month but that it would begin lowering them again in the fourth quarter. Werker-Barak said he expected the next two CPIs to be relatively low.
"Lower interest rates will lead to falling bond yields and more money will come into the stock market," Werker-Barak said.
Super-Sol was the main gainer on the Maof index, rising 2.75 percent to 1,148 agorot (Israeli cents).
In a report released on Monday, Zannex Securities rated the company a buy, saying several factors would strengthen the stock price of the supermarket chain over the next 12 months.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which gained 2.0 percent to 36,807 agorot on volume of 10 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which fell 0.5 percent to 776 agorot on volume of 6.7 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 0.25 percent to 20,036 agorot on turnover of 6.7 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
